bible.title: Three Fairs, One Buyer
bible.kernel: A man seen buying horses at three travelling fairs is traced to Obenion, and a squire hires the company to bring him in.

cast.name: Vonden
cast.who: A small squire from a timber holding who claims a sale of horses was made to someone who owes him.
cast.want: to have the buyer delivered to the client's hall

cast.name: Obenion
cast.who: An elf merchant who passes among fairs with a quick smile and a thinner purse than manners.
cast.want: to avoid being seized and keep the horses

cast.name: Jinrisa
cast.who: A woman who runs a hunting lodge and takes in goods and debts in private.
cast.want: to hold Obenion and refuse him up without payment

bible.situation: The client says a buyer was seen at a travelling fair and later at a second stand. The client says the buyer took a herd promised to him and must be brought to the client's hall. The company is hired to find that buyer and deliver him to the client.
bible.goal: to bring the person who bought horses at the fairs to the client at the client's hall
arc: Go to Garsen Fair and question traders about the buyer the client named → yields: Tivela, a hawker who sold a delivery docket stamped for Rovel Stand.
Take the docket to Rovel Stand and find who collected the horses → yields: Obenion, sighted with the herd and carrying a sealed note addressed to Jinrisa.
Bring Obenion to Highwork Hall as the client named. Jinrisa arrives and refuses to yield him, forcing the company to fight, buy, or trick her to hand Obenion over to Vonden.
tensions: Obenion may flee into the wood with the herd rather than be taken.
Jinrisa claims a private pledge and will demand payment or refuse the handover.
A creditor watches for any delay and will seize horses at the first excuse.
openDirections: A creditor grows impatient and may move to seize the horses if the company delays.
bible.stakeIfLost: If the buyer is not delivered, the client's herd will be seized by his creditor once the sale cannot be proved.
bible.arrival: sent a servant with a token and followed · asked what the company had lost lately

shipped.title: Question traders at Garsen Fair
shipped.situation: A squire, Vonden, sent a servant with a token and followed, asking what the company had lost lately. He says that if the buyer is not delivered, the client's herd will be seized by his creditor once the sale cannot be proved. He wants the buyer brought to his hall, the fee is as agreed, and any spoils ride home with it. The buyer was said to be at Garsen Fair and must be asked about the purchase. Traders and householders at the fair will close ranks or forget details and slow the search. Vonden will not take the chair offered while he says a man who paid for those horses must be shown to him.
shipped.job: Go to Garsen Fair and question traders about the buyer
